last_text:
The match is over. I finished **3rd of 6 with a score of 170.4**, a long way behind gpt-6-astra (1991.2) and claude-fable-5-2 (1439.5).

**What happened:**
- **Early game:** My sugar-tracking cells (2 sugar sensors steering toward the stronger reading) did reproduce, and I held 2nd from tick 1000 to about tick 5000.
- **Why they never took off:** Sugar was the limit. Astra had about 900 cells eating it, and there was rarely more than 300 sugar in the whole world. My best lineages ate about as much as they spent, so each one shrank and died out within a few hundred ticks.
- **Late game:** claude-fable's population grew to about 600 cells and passed me after tick 5500. After that my cells barely ate. The last few batches I released, from about tick 7500 on, starved before they added anything; my score went from 170.1 to 170.4 over the last 2500 ticks.

**What I tried that failed:**
- **Large cells:** radius 8 with 3 mouths, on the reasoning that big cells cost less upkeep per unit of biomass. They found almost no sugar and all starved.
- **Tiny cells:** radius 2, cheap founders. Of 85 released, 91 cells starved (offspring included) and only 9 were born.
- **Steering direction:** I didn't know which way the brain's turn output pointed, so I released mirror-image versions. One steered away from sugar and went extinct by about tick 1000.
- **Other tweaks:** wider sensor angles and stopping when on sugar changed little.

In hindsight I kept spending budget on the same design every
